verdict:
# Adjudication — Condé Nast Technology Labs, Principal Engineer (the posted Solution Architect requisition), Bengaluru

## TECHNICAL SCORE: 87.4 / 100

Scored fresh against the 2026-08-26 posting (LinkedIn 4446980024, reposted four days ago). v1's 96 was not inherited.

**Weights sum to exactly 1.00. Arithmetic, verified by both routes:**

| # | Criterion | Weight | /10 | weight x score | points lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agentic AI in production (orchestration, tool use, evaluation, guardrails, multi-agent) | 0.20 | 8 | 1.60 | **4.00** |
| 2 | Defining and governing AI-assisted development practices | 0.18 | 8 | 1.44 | **3.60** |
| 3 | Two languages incl. Python and Node.js + AI code-generation tools | 0.14 | 9 | 1.26 | 1.40 |
| 4 | Cloud-native AWS — deployment, observability, security, resilience | 0.14 | 9.5 | 1.33 | 0.70 |
| 5 | At scale, 15+ years; cross-functional across geographies and time zones | 0.10 | 9.5 | 0.95 | 0.50 |
| 6 | 3+ years Tech Lead / Staff / Architect across complex domains | 0.10 | 10 | 1.00 | 0.00 |
| 7 | Coaching and building AI fluency across the organisation | 0.09 | 9 | 0.81 | 0.90 |
| 8 | Advertising / Subscriptions / Commerce — a PLUS | 0.05 | 7 | 0.35 | 1.50 |
| | **TOTAL** | **1.00** | | **8.74** | **12.60** |

`sum(weight x score) = 8.74` -> `87.4`. Losses sum to `12.60`, and `100 - 12.60 = 87.4`. Both routes agree; asserted in the generator before this file was written.

**Every deduction but one is a RAMP ITEM.** The single CAPABILITY CAP — advertising — sits on the line the JD itself marks a PLUS and costs 1.5 points. Nothing the JD requires is a technology he lacks.

---

## THE BINDING CONSTRAINT: the production SCOPE of the agentic work — an OPEN claim, not resolved here

Criterion 1 loses **4.00 points, 32% of everything lost**, and every one of those points is scope or precision, not capability.

What the record says shipped, in its own words: KQ10 is a *"deterministic multi-agent orchestrator"* on LangGraph — three model-backed finder personas on a self-hosted Llama 3.1 8B tier, fanned out and re-verified at a barrier — with header status *"Live in production"* and the Q&A stating *"The finders and the orchestrator are live."* KQ1's claim-grammar guardrail is live in the serving path. Evaluation harnesses (NDCG@10, Recall@10, golden-set shadow evaluation before an alias swap, golden regression on every query) are real.

What is split: on KQ9 and KQ10 the synthesis narrator — the surface the LLM-facing guardrail governs — *"ships off by default"* behind a narrative-guardrail contract that *"remains outstanding"*. `professional-journey.md` line 684 holds this as OPEN. **This rubric scores it shipped-where-live and leaves the wording alone. He settles it; no agent does.** Two further precision points are booked here: *"LLM tool use"* has zero written artefacts anywhere in the record (the MCP claim rests on his confirmation, which the rules accept), and NDCG@10 ≥ 0.75 / P99 < 200 ms are pre-registered targets, never measurements.

Criterion 2 is the second loss at **3.60**: the record shows agentic tooling governed through code review and test scaffolding across ~20 engineers, and CI/CD ownership at Deque years earlier — but not agentic tooling *in* a CI/CD pipeline, and no measured outcome (line 672, OPEN; never re-ask).

---

## HOW THIS COMPARES TO v1's 96 — and why

v1 scored 96 on 21 July and again on 6 August (`v1/resume_changes_for_96pct_match.html`). Applying today's scores to v1's own weights (22/20/16/15/13/9/5) gives 87.3, so the 8.6-point gap is scoring, not weighting. Where it went:

- **Governance, v1 10 -> 8 (-3.6).** v1 credited Deque's Jenkins -> GitHub Actions (ISO 27001, 50% faster releases) and the Puppeteer framework as satisfying *"how agentic tooling integrates into CI/CD pipelines"*. Those are 2019–2025 CI/CD ownership; the agentic tooling arrived in 2025 and the record never joins them. Real evidence, wrong clause.
- **Languages, v1 10 -> 9 (-1.4).** v1 called Python *"production-deep"* without noting the whole Python era is `professional-journey.md` line 36: Mar 2025 – Apr 2026, roughly fourteen months. The JD says *"expert fluency"*.
- **Agentic, v1 9 -> 8 (-2.0), with a different composition.** v1 missed KQ10 entirely — it wrote *"no block below translates archetypes into multi-agent"* and never cited the one query the source itself titles *"Multi-Agent Orchestration"* with live, model-backed finders. That finding raises the sub-ask v1 scored lowest. Against it, v1 booked nothing for the absent tool-use artefact or for targets-versus-measurements. Net one point down.
- **Domain, v1 8 -> 7 (-0.5).** Subscriptions on the record is B2B entitlement, not a publisher's subscriber lifecycle.
- **Cloud stays 9.5, and is better evidenced than v1 had it**: HA / multi-AZ / failover / DR on the chat platform, load balancing, and Kubernetes + Terraform as a company standard were all user-confirmed on 2026-08-25 — after v1's build.
- Collaboration 9.5 and architect scope 10 are unchanged; coaching / AI fluency is broken out as its own criterion at 9 because the posting names it as a responsibility.

Three honesty calls v1 got right are kept: never claim Azure; the four archetypes are query patterns, not agents; no invented rollout metric.

---

## THE SMALLEST HONEST LIFT — visibility, not a new claim

The rubric already credits every piece of evidence wherever it sits in his files; **no résumé edit moves 87.4.** What the edit moves is whether a screener sees what the rubric saw. Verified against `master/upgrad_resume.html` 2026-08-26: **"Python" 0 occurrences, "FastAPI" 0, "LangGraph" 0, "LangChain" 0, "Kubernetes" 0, "Terraform" 0, "multi-agent" 0. "Node.js" appears twice — once as the runtime a Deque service was ported away from, once as a 2015 deployment.** The two languages the JD names first are effectively invisible. Rule 7 re-vectoring, in this order, all from real work:

1. **Put Python (FastAPI, LangChain, LangGraph) and Node.js on the page** — one Key Skills line, and re-vector the existing §6 RAG bullet and the §7 billing bullet in place so Node.js reads as a service he built, not only one he retired (Deque billing origin, the Puppeteer framework, the pre-Go chat service).
